## Purpose

One-shot, deploy-time CLI operations run inside the backend container, outside the request
path.

Currently a single script, [bootstrap_admin.py](../../backend/app/scripts/bootstrap_admin.py), which creates the initial administrator
account on a freshly deployed environment where self-registration is disabled and no
authenticated admin exists yet to use the normal `/api/admin/users` path.

## Shape

- [bootstrap_admin.py](../../backend/app/scripts/bootstrap_admin.py) — `check_only()` (exit 0 = users exist, 10 = table empty, 1 = error) and
  `create_admin(email, password)` (exit 0 = created or already-bootstrapped, 1 = error).

  The insert path is one transaction: `_lock_users_table` (Postgres `LOCK TABLE users IN SHARE
  ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE`, no-op on other dialects), re-check `_users_exist` while holding the lock,
  hash via `app.core.security.hash_password`, insert a `User` row with `tier=INITIAL_ADMIN_TIER`
  ("enterprise") and `is_admin=True`, commit.

  The password is read only from stdin (`_read_password_from_stdin`) — **never argv, never an
  env var** — hashed immediately, never logged. `main()` wires `argparse` (`--check-only` xor
  `--email --password-stdin`) to these exit codes for the deploy script to branch on.
- [__init__.py](../../backend/app/scripts/__init__.py) — empty; marks `scripts` as a package.

## Why this shape

The invariant is deliberately narrow: "users table has zero rows → create exactly one
administrator; any row → no-op successfully." Not "no admin exists" — an existing user is never
modified or promoted, and a users-table-with-no-admin state is treated as a recovery scenario
for an audited break-glass procedure, not something this unattended step should backfill on
every deploy.

`COUNT`-then-`INSERT` is a race (two deploy callers could both observe an empty table), so the
write path **takes an explicit table lock** rather than relying on the unique index on `email`
— that index only protects one address, not the "no user existed" invariant globally.

Distinct non-1 exit codes (`10` for "bootstrap required") let `remote-deploy.sh` distinguish
"nothing to do" from "fetch the SSM credential now" from "something is actually broken," so the
password secret is decrypted/transported only on the one deploy where it's genuinely needed.

Nothing else in the backend imports this module — it has no `imported_by` — it is only ever
invoked as `python -m app.scripts.bootstrap_admin` from deploy tooling.
